root_causes.description: product-catalog server-side p99 latency is pinned at the ~10000ms ceiling throughout the incident window while its error rate, CPU usage, memory usage and pod restarts all remain at normal baselines — a pure injected latency fault. As a shared leaf dependency of frontend, checkout and recommendation, the ~10s stall propagates up the call graph, driving frontend p99 to the same ceiling.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 < 100 ms under normal operation
<=0.05 cores; not saturated, ruling out cpu_stress
error_rate < 0.01; latency fault, not error fault

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis: product-catalog CPU saturation inflating response times toward the 10s timeout. Rejected because observed CPU usage is only ~0.027 cores (max 0.040), far below saturation.

frontend p99 is also pinned at 10000ms, but this is downstream-propagation of product-catalog's stall (frontend -> product-catalog edge) rather than an independent fault, since frontend's own error rate is zero and the ceiling is identical.

remediation_steps: Confirm and disable the injected latency fault on product-catalog (flagd fault-injection flag or tc netem / latency sidecar for the seed42 scenario), then roll it back.
Inspect product-catalog request handling for artificial sleeps or downstream I/O stalls to verify the ~10s delay is injected rather than a genuine backend slowdown.
Verify that frontend, checkout and recommendation p99 latency returns below 100ms after the fault is removed, since they are all downstream consumers of product-catalog.
